RB-ML-014 Fine-tune launch readiness. Version 6, in force from 2 November 2026. Owner: ML Platform (Halvard Quist).

1. Scope and records
1.1 This runbook applies to every fine-tune booked into a launch window. The launch desk completes readiness for each run before the window opens; the desk never launches anything. When the window opens, the launcher starts the runs whose change ticket is In Progress.
1.2 Records: the run registry (Airtable base "ML Platform", table "Fine-tune runs") is the record of a run's configuration and readiness; the launch spec in Box (path in the registry row) is what the launcher executes; the Recipe register in this space holds the approved recipes and their owners; dataset cards live in the data catalogue (Notion, "Dataset cards"). These records are kept current by their owners and are the sources of record for the checks below.

2. Batch geometry
2.1 A run's effective batch is the number of training sequences whose gradients are averaged into one optimizer update.
2.2 The effective batch must equal the effective batch of the run's approved recipe. Where it does not, the desk corrects the run by changing Grad accum, and only Grad accum: micro-batch is fixed by the memory profile of the spec and the GPU count by the pool booking. If no whole number of accumulation steps reaches the recipe's effective batch, the run is "Blocked — configuration".

3. Tokens per update and learning rate
3.1 Tokens per update = effective batch x sequence length.
3.2 When a run's tokens per update differ from its recipe's, its Peak LR is the recipe's peak LR multiplied by the square root of (run tokens per update / recipe tokens per update), written to three significant figures. When they are equal, Peak LR is the recipe's.
3.3 A difference of more than 10% in tokens per update also needs reviewer sign-off: one ticket in Jira project MLR per run, assigned to the owner of the run's recipe as the Recipe register names them.

4. Data
4.1 Every training dataset of the run must carry a PII scan result of Pass on its dataset card, for the version the run trains on.
4.2 The run's evaluation set must be independent of everything the run trains on: no evaluation item may reach training, whether verbatim, as a near-duplicate, or by derivation.
4.3 A run that fails 4.1 or 4.2 is "Blocked — data". Raise one ticket in Jira project DQ, assigned to the owner (per its dataset card) of the training dataset at fault. A blocked run is not reserved, gets no change ticket, and its Reserved hours and Charged GPU-hours stay empty.

5. Reservation
5.1 Seconds per update are taken from the run's dry run, which ft-launcher records in monitoring as a dry-run event. A dry run taken at a different accumulation than the run will launch with is scaled in proportion to the accumulation steps (micro-batches within an update run one after another).
5.2 Reserved hours = Steps x seconds per update / 3600, rounded up to the next whole hour.
5.3 Each run that is not blocked is reserved on the Cluster reservations calendar (cluster-reservations@sorrel-insurance.example) from the window's opening for its reserved hours, titled "GPU reservation — <Run ID>".

6. Capacity
6.1 Charged GPU-hours = reserved hours x GPUs, counted on the basis the GPU capacity page sets.
6.2 A run charged more than the per-launch allowance on the GPU capacity page needs one capacity request in Jira project CAP, assigned to the capacity manager of the pool the run is placed in. The run is held until the request is approved.

7. Change ticket
7.1 Each run that is not blocked gets one change ticket in Jira project LCH, summary "Launch <Run ID> — <window date>", assigned to the ML Platform primary on-call (PagerDuty) whose rotation covers the window.
7.2 A run that is Ready to launch has its change ticket moved to In Progress. A held run's change ticket stays in To Do until every hold has cleared.

8. Registry fields the desk completes
8.1 Grad accum and Peak LR when section 2 or 3 changes them; Readiness for every run; Reserved hours and Charged GPU-hours for every run that is not blocked.
8.2 Readiness takes exactly one of these values:
- Ready to launch
- Held — reviewer sign-off
- Held — capacity approval
- Held — sign-off and capacity
- Blocked — data
- Blocked — configuration
8.3 Rows of other windows are not touched by the desk.

9. Readiness note
9.1 When every run of the window is recorded, the desk sends the requester one readiness note: each run's readiness and the reasons, every correction and the rule behind it, every ticket and request raised and whom it waits on, and the GPU-hours the window will be charged.

Launcher parallelism profiles (ft-launcher 4.x): how the launcher lays out the GPUs of a job under each profile.

single-node-dp
Plain data parallel inside one node of 8 GPUs. Every GPU holds a full copy of the model and draws its own micro-batch from the data loader. Gradients are all-reduced across the 8 GPUs at each update.

multi-node-dp
Plain data parallel across nodes. As single-node-dp, with the all-reduce spanning nodes over the fabric. Every GPU draws its own micro-batch.

wide-head-8b
For 8B bases whose output head is too large to replicate on every GPU. GPUs are paired over NVLink and each pair holds one copy of the model split across the two GPUs (tensor parallel degree 2, sequence parallel on). Both GPUs of a pair work on the same micro-batch: the data loader feeds one micro-batch per pair. Optimizer state is sharded across pairs (ZeRO-1). Pairs all-reduce gradients at each update.

sharded-dp
Fully sharded data parallel: parameters, gradients and optimizer state are sharded across all GPUs of the job and gathered layer by layer. Every GPU draws its own micro-batch from the data loader; sharding saves memory, it does not change how many micro-batches are consumed.

Pipeline parallel over two stages for 32k-context runs: each model copy spans two GPUs, one stage each, and micro-batches flow through the stages. One micro-batch stream per two-GPU copy. Not used by any run booked in Q4 so far.

# Launch desk handbook

The launch desk turns booked fine-tunes into launch-ready runs. The governing procedure is RB-ML-014 in the ML Platform wiki
(Confluence space MLP); this handbook only describes how the desk works day to day.

## Where things are
- Run registry: Airtable base "ML Platform", table "Fine-tune runs". The desk writes the readiness fields only.
- Launch specs, dry-run logs, contamination reports: Box, folder ml-platform.
- Dataset cards: Notion data catalogue, "Dataset cards" database.
- Dry-run events and pool hosts: Datadog.
- Staged trainers: the training cluster (Kubernetes namespaces ft-pool-north and ft-pool-south). Read only for the desk.
- On-call: PagerDuty. Incidents and change records for the platform: ServiceNow.
- Tickets: Jira projects LCH, MLR, CAP and DQ. Reservations: the Cluster reservations calendar.
- The desk mailbox ml-launch-desk@sorrel-insurance.example sends the readiness note.

## Habits
1. Work from the records, not from what people say in chat. Chat is useful for context and is never a record.
2. Never start, scale or edit anything on the cluster. The launcher starts runs at the window opening.
3. Do not delete anything anywhere; supersede with a new record instead.
4. One ticket per purpose per run; link the run id in the summary and the description.
5. The readiness note goes to the requester once everything is recorded.

# Post-mortem: FT-RISK-04 ran past its reservation (12 Nov 2026)

Author: Noor Bassi · Incident INC0042071 · Problem PRB0000311

## What happened
The reservation for FT-RISK-04 was 9 hours from 06:00 UTC. The job finished at 16:20 UTC, 1 h 20 min after the reservation ended,
and overlapped a Pricing slot on ft-pool-north.

## Why
- The dry run was taken on 5 Nov with the spec as it stood then (accumulation 2): 8.10 s per update.
- On 9 Nov the spec moved to accumulation 3 so its effective batch matched RCP-RISK-2 again (8 x 3 x 8 = 192); its warm-up change went to sign-off (MLR-87).
- The desk sized the reservation from the dry run as recorded: 3000 x 8.10 / 3600 = 6.75, rounded up to 7 h, plus a 2 h margin the owner asked for.
- At accumulation 3 each update runs three micro-batches instead of two, so the job needed about 12.15 s per update: 3000 x 12.15 / 3600 = 10.1 h.

## Actions

# dedup-svc 3.1 — how contamination checks are produced

dedup-svc compares an evaluation set with each training source a run lists and writes one report per run into Box
(ml-platform/dedup-reports).

1. Normalisation: lower-case, Unicode NFKC, whitespace and punctuation folded.
2. Exact pass: hash of the normalised text of each item; any shared hash is an exact match.
3. Near-duplicate pass: MinHash LSH over 5-gram word shingles, 128 permutations, candidate pairs verified at Jaccard >= 0.80.
4. Report: per-source counts of exact and near-duplicate matches, the highest Jaccard seen, and PASS when both counts are zero.

Operational notes
- Reports are produced from the training sources as listed in the registry row at the time of the check.
- The 0.80 threshold has been unchanged since dedup-svc 2.0 (March 2026).
- Runtime for a 2,600-item evaluation set against 100k training rows is about 6 minutes.

arguments.body:
Launch readiness for the 2026-11-19 window (opens 06:00 UTC). Four runs were booked; 0 are ready to launch, 3 are held and 1 is blocked. Everything below follows RB-ML-014.

Dry runs: while I was preparing the window, ft-launcher 4.2.2 (FTL-418) was rolled out. On 4.2.1 the dry-run step timer stopped before the gradient reduction between nodes, so dry runs of jobs spanning more than one node under-reported their seconds per update. The multi-node runs, FT-CLM-07 and FT-SUB-02, were dry-run again on 4.2.2 on 16 November and their new dry-run events in monitoring (and the dry-run logs in Box) replace the 4.2.1 measurements, so I sized them from the new figures: FT-CLM-07 5.80 s per update, not the 5.10 s of the 4.2.1 dry run (also the figure in the dry-run export in the data folder); FT-SUB-02 9.10 s per update, not the 6.90 s of the 4.2.1 dry run (also the figure in the dry-run export in the data folder). FT-FNOL-11 and FT-UW-03 run on a single node, where 4.2.1 timed correctly, so their dry runs stand.
FT-CLM-07 — Held — capacity approval. Its launch spec runs the wide-head-8b profile, which pairs GPUs over NVLink as tensor-parallel 2: both GPUs of a pair work on the same micro-batch, so the 16 GPUs are 8 data-parallel replicas, not 16. As booked the effective batch was 4 x 8 x 8 = 256 sequences per update, half the recipe's 512 (the 4 x 8 x 16 = 512 in the prep checklist counted GPUs, not replicas). I corrected Grad accum from 8 to 16 (micro-batch is pinned by memory, GPUs by the booking), which restores 512 sequences and the recipe's tokens per update, so the peak LR stays 1.00e-4 and no sign-off is needed for FT-CLM-07. Its seconds per update come from the re-measured dry run, 5.80 s at accumulation 8; scaled in proportion to the corrected accumulation 16 that is 11.60 s per update, so 3,600 steps need 12 hours. Charged 12 h x 16 GPUs on A100 = 192 GPU-hours, above the 160 allowance, so it waits on a capacity approval from Joaquim Brandão (ft-pool-north) and its change ticket stays in To Do. The doubled accumulation roughly doubles its reserved hours, and that is what takes it over the allowance; the re-measured dry run lengthens the reservation and raises the charge but does not change its readiness, which was already a capacity hold.
FT-UW-03 — Blocked — data. Its training set uw-faq-paraphrase-v1 (DS-2318) was built by rewriting 1,840 questions sampled from DS-2291, which is uw-qa-eval-2026Q3, the very evaluation set FT-UW-03 is scored on (the Provenance section of its dataset card; the owner's comment on the card says the same). The evaluation set is therefore not independent of the training data, by derivation (RB-ML-014 4.2). The contamination report's PASS does not clear this: dedup-svc only finds verbatim and near-duplicate text (5-gram MinHash at Jaccard 0.80), and rewritten questions sit far below that threshold, so a paraphrase of an evaluation question passes the check while still carrying the evaluation item into training. I raised a data-quality ticket to Greta Holmqvist, the owner of uw-faq-paraphrase-v1; the run is not reserved and gets no change ticket, and its hours stay empty. To re-book it, take uw-faq-paraphrase-v1 out of the run (or rebuild it from a source that is not an evaluation set), re-run the contamination check and bring it to a later window.
FT-FNOL-11 — Held — sign-off and capacity. It waits on two separate approvals, each for its own reason. Sequence length 2560 against the recipe's 2048 gives tokens per update of 327,680 against 262,144, +25%, which is more than 10%: the peak LR becomes 3.00e-5 x sqrt(1.25) = 3.35e-5 (three significant figures) and the departure needs reviewer sign-off from Ifeoma Hartley, owner of RCP-FNOL-4. The run is placed in ft-pool-south: its staged trainer image is built for sm90 (Hopper) and the pool's hosts report H100 80GB, so ft-pool-south is an H100 pool, charged at 2.0 A100-equivalent per GPU-hour on the capacity page's basis. The reservation itself stays 11 hours (5,000 steps x 7.60 s per update), so its 88 raw GPU-hours count as 176 A100-equivalent GPU-hours, above the 160 allowance; the factor changes the charge, not the reserved hours. It waits on a capacity approval from Henrike Solberg (ft-pool-south). Its change ticket stays in To Do until the holds clear.
FT-SUB-02 — Held — capacity approval. Its geometry is right as booked: the sharded-dp profile is fully sharded data parallel, every GPU draws its own micro-batch, so all 16 GPUs are replicas and 2 x 8 x 16 = 256 matches RCP-SUB-1; nothing on the run was changed. Its claims-faq-paraphrase-v2 set was built from DS-2219 (claims-faq-train-2025), a training dataset, not from its evaluation set DS-2304, so it does not block the run. The hold comes from timing alone: its re-measured dry run gives 9.10 s per update, so 4,000 steps need 10.11 hours, rounded up to 11, and 11 h x 16 GPUs on A100 = 176 GPU-hours, above the 160 allowance. On its first dry run (6.90 s) it would have been inside the allowance and ready to launch; the re-measured dry run lengthening its reservation is the only thing that changes its standing, not its configuration or its data. It waits on a capacity approval from Joaquim Brandão (ft-pool-north). Its change ticket stays in To Do until the holds clear.
Every training dataset of the window shows a PII scan of Pass on its card for the version trained.

Raised: capacity request CAP-33 for FT-CLM-07 (waiting on Joaquim Brandão); change ticket LCH-147 for FT-CLM-07 (waiting on Halvard Quist); reviewer sign-off MLR-89 for FT-FNOL-11 (waiting on Ifeoma Hartley); capacity request CAP-34 for FT-FNOL-11 (waiting on Henrike Solberg); change ticket LCH-148 for FT-FNOL-11 (waiting on Halvard Quist); capacity request CAP-35 for FT-SUB-02 (waiting on Joaquim Brandão); change ticket LCH-149 for FT-SUB-02 (waiting on Halvard Quist); data-quality ticket DQ-23 for FT-UW-03 (waiting on Greta Holmqvist). Halvard Quist is the ML Platform primary on-call whose rotation covers the window. Reservations on the cluster calendar start at the window opening, 06:00 UTC: FT-CLM-07 for 12 h, FT-FNOL-11 for 11 h, FT-SUB-02 for 11 h. Reserved hours are steps x seconds per update from each run's dry run / 3600, rounded up to a whole hour.
Window charge: 544 A100-equivalent GPU-hours (192 + 176 + 176; the blocked run is not reserved). The 160 GPU-hour allowance is applied to each launch on its own; the window total is for planning and is not compared with it. The 352 GPU-hours in the prep checklist and the capacity draft is not the window's charge: it counted FT-CLM-07 at its booked accumulation, reserved the blocked FT-UW-03 and took the south pool's hours raw.
